title: New-window links and scripted popups are silently discarded
impact: Ordinary website links that request another tab do nothing. Popup-based authentication cannot complete through this handler.
recommendation: Separate external website navigation policy from sealed visualization policy. Dispatch ordinary new-tab requests through the service and explicitly support or explain authentication popups.
acceptance: In one local fixture, same-tab navigation, target=_blank, middle-click, and a scripted popup each produce the documented destination or a visible actionable refusal. The opener-based fixture can report a successful callback.

title: Website JavaScript dialogs are always dismissed
impact: An action gated by confirm cannot receive affirmative consent; prompt cannot collect input, and alert messages never reach the operator.
recommendation: Keep sealed visualization restrictions, but supply a native or GPUI dialog bridge for external pages, with a deliberate suppression state when appropriate.
acceptance: A local confirm fixture executes its positive branch after the user chooses OK; Cancel returns false. Prompt returns entered text, and alert is visible. No website can replace the app window.

title: An idle send can clear the only draft before admission fails
impact: An unsent prompt and its staged context can disappear when the user sends to an unavailable workspace or a session that cannot start. This is a conditional loss after accepting Submit, not evidence of general transcript loss.
recommendation: Make send admission return an explicit outcome or recover the full snapshot on every definite refusal. Preserve uncertain-send status separately to avoid accidental duplicate sends.
acceptance: Send a unique multiline prompt with a file and quote after forcing each early refusal. The prompt and context remain editable, the refusal is visible, no user message is falsely shown as delivered, and a later retry sends exactly once. Type a second draft during failure and verify both remain recoverable.

title: A new unsent pane has no durable draft record
impact: A first prompt composed before a thread exists is lost when the app closes. Existing-thread drafts persist, making the difference hard to anticipate. This is loss of unsent editor state before the user accepts Submit, not loss of an accepted prompt or transcript.
recommendation: Persist DraftId-owned records separately from thread drafts, including the launch binding, and migrate ownership atomically on first send.
acceptance: Create two unsent new drafts with different models, branches and attachments. Quit normally and reopen. Both return unchanged; sending one promotes only that draft and does not duplicate it on a second restart.
review_note: A never-sent Cmd+N draft vanished after owned window SIGTERM/restart after autosave; an existing-thread draft persisted and restored as the control. Normal Quit, launch context and attachments were not tested.

title: Ordinary local attachments are not transferred to a remote machine
impact: A local file or pasted screenshot can look attached in a remote thread while the agent receives only a client-local path that does not exist on its machine.
recommendation: Represent ordinary attachment ownership and transfer state explicitly. Stage bytes on the destination before admitting a send, retain progress/errors, and never reinterpret client absolute paths as remote files.
acceptance: Attach a client-only PNG and text file to a remote thread using all three intake methods. The agent can read their exact contents; upload failure retains the draft and offers retry/removal. A coincidentally identical remote path must not substitute different bytes.

title: UI interaction tests do not gate ordinary PR CI
impact: Core tests and an app build can be green while cockpit and pane interaction tests never execute.
recommendation: Run the affected UI crate test targets in required PR CI; retain narrow local verification.
acceptance: A deliberate failing cockpit interaction regression fails the required PR check, and restoring it makes that same check green.

title: Host action bindings take browser and empty-panel input before their local handlers
impact: Browser forms and keyboard navigation cannot rely on normal page input. Enter can send or queue the main conversation draft while the user is editing a web page. Paste targets that draft and takes focus away from the page.
recommendation: Give browser content an explicit input context and route its editing actions to the browser before the cockpit acts. Keep page keys and host navigation shortcuts separate. Guard Submit with the actual sending control or explicit submit intent, so unrelated focused content cannot send its draft.
acceptance: With a fake provider and a local form, leave a sentinel unsent in the main composer. Click the page input and exercise Enter, Tab, Shift-Tab, Escape, copy and paste. The form receives intended keys, the draft remains unchanged, no provider send occurs, and only explicit host commands navigate away.
review_note: The same action-before-key-listener boundary also causes input-focus-002. Browser Enter can send the conversation draft and browser Escape can close the surface. The empty-panel branch was reproduced through real GPUI dispatch: Enter sent PANEL_ENTER_SENTINEL and left the launcher open. The browser branch was not exercised in Chromium. This combined record retains source-proven confidence to avoid presenting both branches as runtime-reproduced.

title: Right-panel tabs, close buttons and PR controls have no keyboard focus or accessible control roles
impact: Keyboard-only users cannot operate much of the right panel. Assistive technology cannot discover the raw controls as named buttons or tabs. A visible hover and an on_click handler do not make a GPUI Div focusable.
recommendation: Use named, focusable native controls for panel actions, with a single tab-order policy. Expose tab state and PR segment selection to accessibility. Preserve focus through redraws rather than just adding handles to controls the focus pump will reclaim. Increase close hit area while retaining the visual icon size.
acceptance: Operate tab switching, close, add, maximize, PR views and PR link without a pointer. Inspect the accessibility tree for names, roles and selected states. Repeated background updates preserve the focused control and Enter/Space executes only that control.

title: Cmd+W on a PR or terminal can close the parent conversation instead of the active panel surface
impact: A familiar close command can remove the working conversation from view when the user intends to close a panel tab. The thread is parked, not deleted, but the navigation change is unrelated to the clicked surface.
recommendation: Route close through a focused-area owner and active surface. Preserve the explicit command for closing a conversation, with a clearly named separate action or context.
acceptance: For each panel surface, focus its content, press close once and assert only its tab closes. The parent thread stays selected and unparked. Test the browser/file/review exceptions to preserve their existing behavior.

title: Typing y, n or a as the first character of an empty approval composer performs a permission action
impact: A user who starts a normal follow-up with "also", "no" or "yes" can answer a pending approval before sending a message. The a shortcut means Always. This is an intentional current interaction contract, but it conflicts with the live text-field affordance.
recommendation: Keep bare approval letters in an explicitly focused approval region or non-editing mode. Use modified chords or ordinary focused buttons while the composer is editable. Preserve question and nonempty-draft behavior.
acceptance: With an approval pending and the composer empty, type "also check this", "no, change direction" and "yes, after tests" as ordinary key events. All text remains unsent and no approval response occurs. Explicit approval shortcuts and buttons still work.

title: Files editor and filter lose keyboard focus when their edits redraw the cockpit
impact: Code editing and file filtering can redirect subsequent typing into the main conversation. This is a concrete missing exemption in the current focus reconciliation, beyond the broader area-navigation gap in input-focus-005.
recommendation: Preserve the active Files editor and filter as real focus owners. Prefer a general active-surface ownership check over another loosely related global exception. Replace the editing proof with a rendered click-and-type integration check in addition to the autosave test.
acceptance: In a scratch checkout, click a source line and type several separate key events across cockpit updates. Assert every character lands in the file, none enters the composer, and focus remains in the editor. Repeat in the file filter and while a transcript streams. No live user file is needed for this test.
review_note: Real clicks followed by separate printable keys sent xyz and sam to the main composer; the editor and filter remained unchanged. Failure was visible on the first post-click key.

title: A failed file save is silent and closing the file discards the edited buffer
impact: An operator can lose unsaved work when the file becomes unwritable or its parent directory disappears. P0 follows this audit's data-loss rule; this is conditional, not a claim that ordinary saves fail.
recommendation: Return structured save results, report failures, keep the tab and draft on failure, and make close/save decisions explicit. Use atomic replacement to avoid partial-write corruption.
acceptance: In a disposable checkout, deny writes after editing. Save displays the filesystem error. Closing preserves the exact draft and offers retry or explicit discard. Restore permission and verify that retry writes the draft.
review_note: Conditional loss of an edited buffer remains urgent. P0 was too strong without a reproduced widespread trigger.

title: Cached editor buffers can overwrite newer agent or other-thread changes
impact: An agent and operator often edit the same checkout. A later save from an old file buffer can erase the agent's changes. Two Ferrite threads pointing at one checkout also create independent buffers.
recommendation: Track disk revisions, refresh clean buffers on workspace changes, and block or reconcile conflicting saves. Coordinate writes by canonical workspace and file, not by thread alone.
acceptance: Open the same file in two threads sharing a checkout. Change a different line in each, and repeat with an external agent edit. No successful save silently removes the other edit; a conflict is visible and recoverable.
review_note: A stale buffer can overwrite an agent's newer disk contents. This is a Ferrite integrity defect. The independent reviewer did not find T3 stale-write protection either, so it is not presented as a verified T3 parity advantage. A clean Markdown preview stayed stale on same-tab revisit after external replacement; close/reopen loaded new disk text. Dirty-buffer overwrite and save-conflict loss were not exercised.

title: The file tree never refreshes cached directory entries or Git status
impact: Files created, deleted, or renamed by an agent are missing or stale in an already opened tree. Git colors remain based on its initial snapshot.
recommendation: Invalidate directories and Git status on workspace mutation and expose Refresh. Keep expanded paths and selection while applying updates.
acceptance: With Files already open, create, rename, delete, and modify files through a terminal or agent. Tree rows and status update without restarting or changing threads; manual refresh also works.
review_note: External add/delete left cached children unchanged even after collapse/re-expand. Git status coloring is not runtime-tested.

title: Nested file tabs overflow into an inaccessible clipped region
impact: Opening many files can put the active file's tab and close control offscreen. The unified panel strip's overflow controls do not control this separate strip.
recommendation: Move editable files into the shared panel surface list. If retaining an inner strip, add overflow navigation and automatic active-tab reveal with the same keyboard and close semantics.
acceptance: Open 20 kept files at a narrow panel width. Reach, activate, and close every tab by mouse and keyboard. A newly opened or reactivated file always has a visible selected tab.
review_note: Eighteen kept inner tabs placed files-tab-17 at x=3250 in a 1440px window without strip navigation. The file tree still activates paths; the failure concerns strip access and hidden close controls.

title: Changes cuts each file at 120 displayed lines with no expansion action
impact: A primary review view hides later changes in a large file. A user can mark the file reviewed without having a way to inspect its omitted hunks in that view.
recommendation: Give Changes a full diff renderer with lazy hunk loading or virtualization. Keep summary caps only in explicitly abbreviated Overview cards.
acceptance: Create a diff with more than 200 changed lines and a distinctive deletion near the end. The user can inspect that deletion in Changes and reach every omitted hunk before marking the file reviewed.

title: Terminal startup failures leave no visible result
impact: Terminal is a primary debugging fallback. A failed shell launch makes its menu item and shortcut look broken.
recommendation: Represent terminal startup as loading, running, or failed. Retain the failed surface so the operator can read the error and retry.
acceptance: Force a shell or cwd startup failure in a disposable thread. Both the menu and shortcut display the same actionable failure and recover after fixing the cause.

title: Clicking another thread's PR routes to a panel that is not shown
impact: A plain click on the underlined PR badge of a nonfocused thread does not reveal its destination. The browser request targets that thread, while the visible panel remains attached to the focused thread. If browser ownership is unavailable, attachment fails and its error is also stored under the hidden target. This directly explains a class of apparent dead sidebar links.
recommendation: Route an explicit PR click through a destination-aware navigation operation that makes the clicked thread or selected PR visible. Keep agent-initiated browser reveals separate from explicit user navigation.
acceptance: With A focused and B visible in the sidebar, click B's PR number. B's exact PR becomes visible on that click. Repeat with B without a board pane, with the panel hidden, and from the empty board. A modifier click opens the external URL without switching the thread.
review_note: Actual production gh discovery in two scratch repositories plus rendered badge clicks reproduced A selected / B clicked / no visible destination. The focused-thread badge was a positive control. CEF page load was not tested.

title: PR detail stays stale after status refresh and agent actions
impact: Users cannot trust the displayed checks, comments, description, or generated guide to reflect the current PR. A running check can remain running after completion.
recommendation: Give detail a refresh command and invalidation keyed by repository, PR and head/revision. Refresh activity after writes and checks while pending. Preserve a timestamp and stale state.
acceptance: Open a PR with a pending check, finish the check remotely, add a comment, and invoke Refresh PR status. The same panel shows the new result and comment. A new guide appears after its agent completes without reopening the PR.
review_note: Both menu and palette Refresh PR status left same-number/same-lifecycle detail checks/body/comments stale while lightweight state updated. Re-entry and OPEN→MERGED refresh worked. Agent-action invalidation is not runtime-tested.

title: Create PR is unavailable for branch work absent from the current thread transcript
impact: A user who opens a prepared branch, makes manual edits, or imports work from another session cannot use the native Create PR button unless this thread has recorded file edits.
recommendation: Offer Create PR from repository state or a stable command, independent of transcript-derived change cards. Preserve the current agent handoff if that is the chosen creation design.
acceptance: Open a fresh thread on a branch with an ahead-of-base commit created outside Ferrite. Create PR is discoverable and targets that branch. No synthetic agent edit is required.

title: Rename on Parked and Snoozed rows creates an editor that is never drawn
impact: An advertised rename action cannot be completed visibly on either slim shelf. The root also attempts to focus the absent editor, which creates a keyboard reliability risk.
recommendation: Pass the same editable title into full and slim rows. Focus it only after the row has rendered. Keep Enter and Escape on the visible editor.
acceptance: Right-click a Parked row and a Snoozed row, choose Rename, and see the existing title in a focused field. Type, save, reopen the app, and confirm the saved title. Escape must cancel without swallowing subsequent navigation keys.
review_note: Rendered Snoozed-row Rename closed the menu but displayed no editor or rename hint; the stored title remained unchanged. Parked remains source-only. Working-row commit was inconclusive and is not counted as a save failure.

title: Approval cards can state the wrong Codex sandbox
impact: The operator can approve a command while the card claims a more restrictive sandbox than the process actually has. This is an incorrect permission description, not evidence that Ferrite escapes the provider sandbox.
recommendation: Project the negotiated sandbox through session events, thread state and the wire snapshot, and render that value. Keep requested defaults distinct from effective values.
acceptance: With a stub Codex handshake returning workspaceWrite while Settings is CLI default, an actual clicked approval card says workspace-write. Change the default to read-only and verify the existing card remains workspace-write. Repeat for a remote thread and dangerFullAccess. No real destructive command is needed.

title: Remote permission and server defaults save to the local machine
impact: On an SSH machine, settings can appear saved while new remote sessions continue using the remote server's old permission and sandbox defaults. Factory concurrency and other server-side preferences have the same ownership problem.
recommendation: Separate window preferences from server settings. Add a targeted server-settings read/write operation with an acknowledgement and display the machine whose defaults are edited. Do not silently synchronize unrelated local values.
acceptance: Use two isolated settings directories with different permission/sandbox defaults. Through a remote window change one default, create a thread and inspect its provider launch arguments/handshake. Only the selected machine changes, relaunch retains it, and denied/offline writes display an unsaved state.

title: Agent transcript prose clips at ordinary panel width
impact: At a 420px panel, child transcript sentences lose their endings beyond the right edge. Maximizing to 960px reveals the complete text. Output arrival alone does not make the agent screen readable.
recommendation: Measure and wrap child prose against the actual panel content width; retain reading position across maximize, restore and resize. The precise layout cause remains to be isolated.
acceptance: Open a child with ordinary multi-sentence output at minimum and ordinary widths. Every character remains readable without maximizing; resizing and restoring reflow existing output without waiting for another event.
review_note: Parent inspected both screenshots. Source references locate the rendering path; they are not a proven root cause or proposed patch.

title: Browser retains a duplicate heading, nested tabs and legacy card beneath shared panel tabs
impact: The Browser surface row is followed by a second Browser title, a page-tab strip and then the toolbar. Repeated identities, differently scoped plus controls and competing frames consume space and make the existing browser look unfinished.
recommendation: Complete the shared surface model: give each page one clear identity and unify tab/control density; remove the redundant legacy Browser heading/card layer where the panel already provides it.
acceptance: Open one and two pages, switch to Files and back, and close the active page. Active identity and add/close scope remain clear, with a single deliberate panel hierarchy and aligned content edges.
review_note: Chrome observed in headless screenshots and personally in installed Ferrite with a loaded example.com page. The unavailable headless page body is expected and is not counted as a native browser-load defect. This is a visual-quality judgment supported by actual assembly and ADR 0039.

title: Cite has no reachable per-quote comment editor
impact: The user cannot attach their own words to an individual citation. Multiple citations cannot each receive an independently editable instruction. The ordinary composer remains a separate place to type general text; this finding does not establish that all typing after Cite is broken.
recommendation: Add a native comment editor to the citation interaction, with Save, Cancel, multiline input, a focus return target and a later Edit comment action. Keep quote source and user comment separate. Correct composer.md's positive claim that reply cards already provide a usable commenting workflow.
acceptance: Using only UI actions, cite two different passages, add different multiline comments, edit one, cancel another edit, add general prompt text, reopen the draft and send. Each comment remains editable and paired with its quote. IME Enter does not save or send prematurely. A quote with no comment also sends.
review_note: The user explicitly requires adding their own text to a citation. This is a required workflow gap, not an optional feature candidate. Clean pointer Cite and ordinary composer annotation worked, sending exactly > amber followed by My clean annotation. Clicking the quote tile exposed no editor; typing there was unhandled. This is a per-quote authoring gap, not proof that ordinary text cannot accompany a quote.

title: Quoted file and skill syntax can become active provider input
impact: Citing reference text can attach a local file or activate a Codex skill even though the user only meant to discuss the quoted text. A quote can therefore change the provider input beyond its visible citation card.
recommendation: Carry typed context to provider adapters and expand quotation text only as text. At minimum isolate quoted material from attachment and skill scanning. Use the annotation encoder's explicit separation as an existing design precedent, not a blanket text replacement that corrupts quoted content.
acceptance: Against a fake provider and harmless fixture files, cite exact file/skill syntax and inspect the wire payload. It contains the unchanged reference text but no unsolicited file bytes, localImage, localAudio, mention or skill item. Explicitly attaching the same fixture still produces the intended typed item.

title: The reported pointer Cite regression still needs installed-app reproduction
impact: The user reports that citing no longer works. Existing event handlers and fixture tests do not establish that the installed app accepts the real selection and reaches the composer.
recommendation: Parent should capture the installed build identity, selection, toolbar, click result and focus destination. Keep the report open until that reproduction distinguishes no offer, dead activation, wrong destination and inability to type. Do not mark the regression fixed because a handler exists.
acceptance: On the installed build, test plain prose, code, tables, links, double/triple click, cross-block selection, scrolling, a narrow pane, right-panel focus and two open threads. Verify the citation reaches the intended draft and typing works. Record pointer coordinates and before/after evidence for every failure. Do not send to a live provider without an appropriate disposable thread.
review_note: The isolated pinned-source build did not reproduce the blanket pointer Cite failure. A clean selection, Cite, ordinary text entry and send succeeded. The installed intermittent symptom remains unresolved, and this verification-gap record stays unverified.

title: Nested agents and immediate-parent navigation are missing from the normal drill path
impact: The core knows grandchildren, but inspecting a child loses the routes needed to inspect its children or identify the immediate parent.
recommendation: Pass child mappings into agent transcripts, route OpenAgent from a Drill to another Drill, and expose immediate-parent and root navigation using AgentInfo.parent. Add a relationship list independent of retained spawn rows.
acceptance: Create Main > A > B with both providers. Open A from Main, then B from A. B identifies A as parent, opens A, and offers Main separately. Completed children remain reachable after spawn rows are outside the rendered window.
review_note: Controlled Main > Alpha > Grandchild rendered nested controls; both nested row and View live output did nothing. This verifies the normal drill failure, not every parent/ancestry/provider path.

title: Reopen closed tab restores empty Agent and SideChat tabs
impact: The advertised reopen action returns a blank subagent view.
recommendation: Reconstruct the agent resource through open_agent_drill when reopening its SurfaceId, or exclude it from reopen until a resource-aware restore exists.
acceptance: Open an agent with visible text, close its tab, then invoke Reopen closed tab. The same agent and transcript return. Repeat through Close all and confirm each restored tab has content.
review_note: Both paths restore a tab identifier after releasing its backing view. File previews are excluded because their renderer hydrates them on reopen. Both Agent and SideChat close/reopen failures were exercised through real controls. Reopen returns the tab identity with no backing body. File previews remain excluded.

title: Right-click has no browser context menu
impact: Operators cannot discover normal link, image, selection, and editable-field actions through right-click.
recommendation: Introduce a browser-specific context menu using native hit-test details. Do not apply arbitrary website menus to sealed content.
acceptance: Right-click a link and copy its destination; right-click selected page text and copy it; paste into an input through the menu. Each action operates on the clicked page.

title: Browser tabs discard page titles and show only hostnames
impact: Two pages on the same host, including two localhost apps on different ports, have indistinguishable tab labels. Favicons are absent.
recommendation: Carry page identity metadata through service state and render title, favicon, and a full-address tooltip. Keep port in the fallback.
acceptance: Tabs titled Docs and Dashboard on one origin remain distinguishable; two untitled localhost ports show distinct fallback labels. Title changes update the correct tab.

title: Address entry rejects normal schemeless hostnames
impact: Common development addresses such as localhost:3000 require manual http:// entry.
recommendation: Normalize human address input separately from the service authorization policy. Do not weaken scheme restrictions or silently turn arbitrary text into a network destination.
acceptance: localhost:3000 opens http://localhost:3000; example.com opens https://example.com. Explicit unsupported schemes still produce clear errors.

title: Page navigation can overwrite an unfinished address edit
impact: A redirect or same-page URL change can replace the address the user is currently typing.
recommendation: Introduce explicit address editing state. Show committed URL while idle; preserve and validate the draft while editing; Escape should restore the committed URL.
acceptance: Type a new URL during a delayed redirect and a history.pushState update. The draft survives both. Escape restores the final page URL, and Enter navigates to the draft.

title: New-tab mode leaves navigation controls pointed at the hidden old page
impact: Clicking Reload or Back while an empty new tab is shown unexpectedly acts on the previous tab and abandons new-tab entry.
recommendation: Model the displayed target explicitly or consistently derive toolbar state from the displayed page. Keep draft new-tab state independent of the previous document.
acceptance: After clicking plus, Back, Forward, and Reload cannot affect the old page. The address draft remains until explicit submission, cancel, or tab selection.

title: Loading changes browser geometry and shifts the address field
impact: Loading moves the page and changes its actual viewport size. The Annotate button also appears and disappears, changing address width.
recommendation: Reserve one compact navigation row; keep annotation visible but disabled during loading and place progress in an overlay or fixed-height track.
acceptance: Record the page origin, page viewport size, and address bounds before and during a slow navigation. All remain stable, and loading remains visible. Narrow-width controls stay operable.
review_note: Parent native observations corroborated the loading branch: Annotate disappeared, Address shifted left and a Loading row appeared above the page. The installed commit is unknown and captures are conversation-only. The source finding remains source-proven; no timing, focus, controlled slow-load or network-error sequence was certified.

title: Viewport size is inseparable from panel size
impact: The operator cannot verify a site at a precise mobile or desktop viewport, rotate a preset, or compare a large layout while keeping the chat readable.
recommendation: Add a user-selected viewport mode distinct from host size and device pixel ratio, plus explicit page zoom. Validate dimensions and preserve selection per browser tab.
acceptance: A 390 by 844 preset reports those CSS dimensions in the page while the right panel is resized; rotate swaps dimensions; Fill restores host-sized layout. Zoom has a visible reset.

title: Find, DevTools, hard reload, and page appearance controls are absent
impact: Long-page search and normal web development inspection require leaving the embedded browser. Cache bypass and theme checks have no operator controls.
recommendation: Add typed page operations and a browser menu. Keep find scoped to the website rather than transcript search; surface supported runtime distinctions.
acceptance: Find highlights matches and cycles next/previous in the current page; DevTools targets the correct tab; hard reload bypasses a fixture cache; light/dark setting updates a media-query fixture.

title: Inactive-page reclamation restores only a URL, losing navigation and page position
impact: A clean tab can lose its Back/Forward stack, scroll position, and transient UI state merely because it was hidden. Restart also restores only URLs and selection.
recommendation: Preserve native tabs for normal switching or retain a navigation/session snapshot before reclaiming. Define the resource policy explicitly instead of immediate hidden-state disposal. Do not claim full T3 session restoration without checking its host lifetime.
acceptance: Visit A then B, scroll B, switch away and back through actual reclamation, and verify Back returns to A and B restores its scroll. Repeat after restart according to the documented persistence contract.

title: An empty browser provides neither useful guidance nor recent/local destinations
impact: Opening the browser or a new tab leaves the user to recover a URL manually from terminal output or memory.
recommendation: Render an actual empty/new-tab page with address guidance, scoped recent destinations, and discovered local servers. Reuse existing terminal/server discovery if available rather than introducing another scanner.
acceptance: First open and last-tab close show guidance. Starting a local development server yields a clearly labeled destination, and a recently visited URL can be reopened and removed.

title: Persistent website profiles have no operator management controls
impact: Cookies survive sessions, but the operator cannot clear broken authentication/cache or choose isolated browser identities from the browser UI.
recommendation: First add visible active-profile identity and scoped clear-cookie/cache operations. Treat multi-profile, private sessions, and cookie import as separate product choices; do not import credentials without an explicit user action.
acceptance: A fixture cookie persists normally, clears through the named profile action, and stays isolated from another chosen profile if multi-profile support is adopted. The UI states which data will be cleared.

title: Browser capture is annotation-oriented and lacks direct recording/export affordances
impact: An operator cannot directly record a browser interaction or capture a plain screenshot through the browser chrome for external sharing.
recommendation: Reuse the existing capture pipeline for a plain screenshot command with output feedback. Decide recording scope separately; show active recording and its destination rather than hiding it behind a modifier-only gesture.
acceptance: A direct screenshot contains the current page at the chosen scale and can be opened from the reported destination. If recording is added, start/stop yields a playable file with a visible active-state indicator.

title: No browser-chrome escape to the system browser
impact: When a website needs unsupported authentication, downloads, permissions, or development tools, the operator must manually copy the address and leave the app.
recommendation: Add Open in system browser for the committed page URL, with an error if launching fails. Do not send the unsubmitted address draft.
acceptance: The action opens the current page in the configured browser; an unfinished address draft does not change the launched destination.

title: Queued Edit removes the message and merges it into unrelated draft text
impact: Editing a queued message changes queue membership immediately and combines it with a separate draft. There is no save-in-place or cancel that restores both original pieces of work.
recommendation: Either rename this operation Take back and disclose its merge behavior, or add transactional queued editing with independent draft storage and a provider/server edit operation.
acceptance: With queued A/B and draft C, edit A and cancel: A/B order and C remain unchanged. Repeat and save A2: only A changes, C is restored, and no extra turn is started. Cover A starting while its edit is open.
review_note: Real queued-edit click canceled the queued UUID and combined QUEUED_SENTINEL with UNRELATED_DRAFT. Both texts survived; their independent identities did not. Multi-item and race branches remain untested.

title: The composer cannot choose queue versus steer per message
impact: Users cannot deliberately defer a follow-up until the current turn finishes. A message intended as later work can alter the running turn.
recommendation: Add an explicit dispatch intent through UI, protocol and provider adapters. Keep a local/default behavior preference with a one-shot alternate action.
acceptance: In both providers, Queue leaves the running turn unmodified and starts only after it ends; Steer reaches the running turn. Pointer tooltip, modifier-click, keyboard and accessibility label describe the same action. Unsupported steer never appears available.

title: Stop deliberately allows queued work to continue
impact: A user expecting Stop to stop automation can see queued work start immediately. This is intentional current code behavior, not an accidental missing interrupt.
recommendation: Make stopping semantics an explicit product decision. Prefer a hold state that survives restart, with Resume and separately named Send now behavior.
acceptance: With pending A/B, Stop visibly acknowledges interruption and neither A nor B runs until Resume. If retaining current semantics, the label and confirmation-free explanatory text must clearly state that queued work will continue.

title: Attachment readiness and native-image fallbacks are invisible
impact: A chip can imply that a model received an image even when it got only a path. Missing or oversized files have no composer warning. HEIC/HEIF is not a native image format in the provider attachment classifier.
recommendation: Add provider-aware validation and explicit attachment state, including a visible file-reference fallback. Prepare images off the UI thread, and retain original bytes where needed.
acceptance: Each boundary case produces either a ready native image or a visible explanation before Send. Deleted/unreadable files block or require removal. HEIC is converted or clearly labeled as a file. The agent sees the expected image bytes for accepted inputs.

title: Large pastes stay inline with no composer length guard
impact: Large logs or documents fill the prompt directly and can hit provider or transport limits without an early actionable message. No performance regression is claimed without measurement.
recommendation: Add a provider-aware send limit and optional large-paste-to-file path, retaining an editable override. Do not copy T3 numeric limits blindly.
acceptance: A large paste becomes a named readable text attachment with feedback; the override preserves inline text. Oversize sends do not clear content and explain how to proceed. Test Unicode byte/character boundaries and selection replacement.

title: Context is mostly a shelf or serialized trailer rather than inline records
impact: Users cannot place an image, quote, review note or browser annotation at a precise point in instructions, move it as one inline object, or copy the object with its context to another draft.
recommendation: Introduce structured context records while keeping a plain-text fallback for providers. Preserve positions and clipboard metadata without requiring every attachment to become a new visual component.
acceptance: Write instructions around two image chips and a quote; cut/paste them into a second draft and restart. Each preview, source and relative position survives, and the outgoing prompt identifies the intended object correctly.

title: The mention menu has no PR, thread or model-reference search
impact: Users must manually find and describe another thread, PR or model. Structured references that an agent can inspect on demand are missing from the composer.
recommendation: Add reference-specific item types and payloads. Reuse PR/thread identity from their owning modules rather than scraping displayed text. Keep linked-machine transport separate from local thread references.
acceptance: Pick a PR by number and text, a thread by title, and a model by alias. Each chip previews the right source; model mention leaves active model unchanged; the agent receives a resolvable reference. A sidebar thread drop has the same result as a menu pick.

title: Review comment drafts lose their structured controls after reopen
impact: Review comments survive as prose but no longer have their original review attachment controls after the pane is recreated. This is loss of editability and source structure, not loss of the comment words.
recommendation: Persist comments separately from outbound prompt text and hydrate them with the other draft context records.
acceptance: Add two anchored review comments, restart, and remove just one through its original control. The remaining comment retains its file/line anchor and sends once; neither appears as duplicated raw export text.

title: Some UI tests bypass real keyboard and opener dispatch
impact: Direct handler calls can pass when binding precedence, focus or the visible opener prevents the user reaching that handler.
recommendation: Add real click/key regression paths with production bindings, normal viewport and a populated composer. Keep helper tests but do not count them as entry-point verification.
acceptance: Empty-panel Enter opens its highlighted panel without sending a prompt. Each PR entry point visibly opens its intended target through normal event dispatch.

title: Required-form editability coverage never proves valid typed submission
impact: The negative-only test can pass if typing never edits the required field, because both an invalid value and an untouched empty field are rejected.
recommendation: Type a valid value through the real field, repaint, submit, assert the exact typed answer and unchanged composer.
acceptance: A typed 2 survives repaint and reaches the correct decision as integer 2; invalid 9 produces a visible error and no answer.

title: Default UI checks do not establish native Chromium behavior
impact: Synthetic browser frames and a non-CEF app build cannot prove native page input, focus transfer, navigation or frame delivery.
recommendation: Use a feature-aware native smoke gate for browser changes against a local fixture page and temporary profile.
acceptance: A CEF-enabled app accepts a real page-input click, text and Enter; back/forward change the visible document; host focus returns correctly. Fake-engine tests cannot satisfy this gate.

title: Window geometry still resets at launch
impact: Users must repeatedly resize and reposition Ferrite because launch always supplies centered 1440 by 900 bounds.
recommendation: Persist normal bounds and maximized state, validate restored geometry against attached displays, and use a fitting fallback.
acceptance: Temporary-profile relaunch restores usable size, position and maximization; a disconnected saved monitor never strands the window.

title: CLI help advertises variadic provider arguments that the parser rejects
impact: Parent reproduced a provider launch failure when following the apparent list syntax. Repeated --args flags work, but help does not make that invocation clear.
recommendation: Print repeatable-list syntax and a provider-argument example in generated help, or explicitly define a trailing passthrough boundary. Correct callers relying on unsupported syntax.
acceptance: The generated thread-start help example parses to args ["--model", "fable", "--effort", "high"] without launching a provider; unknown Ferrite flags retain precise errors.

title: No workspace-area focus cycle or per-surface focus restoration connects the composer and panel
impact: Users who enter the terminal or panel cannot rely on one keyboard command to move among major areas. Opening or switching a panel tab does not establish a consistent focus handoff. Focus behavior depends on the specific body component.
recommendation: Introduce explicit focus ownership for major visible areas and a remembered focus target per panel surface. Route keyboard focus deliberately on open, switch and close. Keep the composer's useful local tool walk, but provide a separate area-navigation command.
acceptance: F6 and Shift-F6, or documented equivalents, visit visible nav, conversation, composer and panel areas. They leave a terminal and browser without typing into them. Reopening a tab restores its last valid control. A closed or hidden tab never retains focus.

title: Embedded browser input has no composition or native text-input bridge
impact: Users of input methods, composed text and native text services lack an implemented path equivalent to Ferrite's composer. Sending raw key_char values is not a composition protocol. Exact failures for each operating-system input method need runtime checks.
recommendation: Implement native text-input and composition for the offscreen browser, including caret bounds and commit/cancel handling. Do not treat synthetic per-key CHAR events as sufficient. Audit the custom terminal input path separately because it also reads raw key events.
acceptance: Compose and commit a Japanese phrase and Chinese candidate sequence in a local browser textarea on each supported OS. Cancel a composition with Escape, move the candidate cursor, and confirm no host command runs and the candidate window follows the caret.

title: Panel resizing relies on root hover events that occluding children can block
impact: A resize drag may stall over the panel edge or another occluding control and may miss its release. This is a source-backed risk, not a measured or runtime-reproduced failure.
recommendation: Use an explicit captured drag session or capture-phase window listeners with an active-drag guard. End it on release, cancellation, window blur and owner disappearance. Confirm the actual failure before selecting the smallest repair.
acceptance: Resize continuously across the edge, tabs, browser and terminal. Release outside the original edge and outside the window. Width follows continuously and never changes after release. Include slow movement smaller than the edge width.

title: Find in a Files editor searches the conversation instead of the file
impact: Users searching the code or prose currently visible in Files get a transcript search. The shortcut changes the wrong reading context and does not offer file-local matching.
recommendation: Route Find through the focused surface and implement a file-local search owner for code and prose. Keep transcript search scoped to conversation focus.
acceptance: Use a file containing a sentinel absent from the transcript. Focus the file and invoke Find. The sentinel matches and scrolls into view in the file; the transcript search remains closed. Repeat for Markdown and after returning from another panel tab.
review_note: Cmd+F after clicking the file editor opened transcript Find and highlighted a transcript match in the pinned headless build.

title: Transcript web-link menus cannot explicitly open the system browser
impact: Users cannot choose their normal browser, authenticated profile or extensions from the link itself. The only Open action requests Ferrite Browser. Copying and manually pasting the address is the available escape.
recommendation: Add an explicit system-browser verb to the shared link interaction, preserving the resolved address. Name browser destinations consistently. This is separate from BROWSER-16, which owns opening the already active browser page externally.
acceptance: Right-click [Example](https://example.com/a?b=c#d). Open in system browser launches that exact URL without creating or selecting a Ferrite tab. Open in integrated browser opens it in the owning thread. Copy link address copies the URL, not Example. Repeat while text is selected and while streaming.
review_note: The actual transcript menu showed Open link and Copy link, with no explicit system-browser action. The installed copy-only symptom was not reproduced on this fixture. No browser navigation outcome was tested.

title: Modified and middle clicks on transcript web links ignore destination intent
impact: Cmd/Ctrl-click and middle-click cannot bypass Ferrite Browser. The same gesture works differently on a sidebar PR badge, creating an unpredictable everyday navigation rule.
recommendation: Resolve link activation once from target, button, modifiers and user preference. Keep the gesture distinct from browser-page target=_blank handling, already owned by BROWSER-01. T3 supports a saved app/system preference; Ferrite can choose a different default without ignoring overrides.
acceptance: Exercise plain, Cmd/Ctrl, Shift and middle clicks on the same transcript URL and sidebar PR. Assert the documented destination and whether selection changes. Dragging still selects without opening, and right-click never navigates.

title: Issue-reference context menus open and copy an internal scheme instead of the real URL
impact: A generated #212 reference can work on left click but fail through Open link. Copy link yields issue:212 rather than a shareable repository issue URL.
recommendation: Represent resolved target identity separately from display text and internal renderer schemes. Share decoding between clicks, menus and copy. Audit ferrite-path:, ferrite-thread:, ferrite-chip: and ferrite-skill: at the same boundary; do not advertise OS actions for app-only targets.
acceptance: For origin git@github.com:owner/repo.git and #212, plain click and both browser menu actions use https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/212; Copy link address copies that URL. Missing origin produces an unavailable reason rather than issuing issue:212 to the OS.

title: Custom file chips lose target-aware context actions
impact: An inline source-file chip supports opening but lacks reliable right-click actions for its full path, relative path, editor or file manager. A user cannot copy the actual destination from an abbreviated label with the confidence provided by a normal URL link.
recommendation: Pass a typed file target through custom rendering and install its own context menu. Offer Copy full path and Copy relative path where meaningful, Open in Files at the referenced line, and supported editor/reveal actions. Keep display-label copying as text selection.
acceptance: Right-click a chip whose visible label differs from its path. Copy full/relative path returns the intended path with documented position suffix. Open in Files reveals line 42. Repeat after right-clicking an unrelated URL to ensure no stale target is reused, and for missing files and image chips.
review_note: Right-clicking the rendered sample.rs chip opened whole-message Copy, Attach, Pin and Fork actions, with no file-target actions.

title: Markdown section links are sent to the OS instead of scrolling within the document
impact: Tables of contents and section references in generated explanations or plans do not navigate to their headings.
recommendation: Add document-scoped heading identity and fragment navigation before file or external URL dispatch. Preserve a stable heading target across streaming updates and avoid selecting a heading in another answer with the same name.
acceptance: A local fixture with two answers containing Details headings scrolls to the clicked answer's heading. Percent-encoded fragments and duplicate heading suffixes work. Missing anchors give a defined result and never launch an external application.

title: Ordinary Markdown links and their transcript menus have no keyboard activation path
impact: Keyboard users cannot traverse and activate the same web links available to pointer users, or choose a link menu action after opening the pointer-only transcript menu.
recommendation: Give inline links stable focusable semantic targets and reuse the app's accessible menu implementation. Keep this scoped to transcript links; input-focus-003 already owns right-panel control accessibility.
acceptance: Without a pointer, focus a link, activate it with Enter, open its context menu and choose Open in system browser or Copy address. Escape closes the menu and restores link focus. Re-rendering streaming text does not lose the focused target or submit the composer.
review_note: Escape left the open link menu visible after real key dispatch. This proves the dismissal failure in the tested state; the broader keyboard-activation claim remains source-proven.

title: Right-clicking a sidebar PR badge can offer Copy link for the thread instead of the PR
impact: A user who right-clicks an underlined PR number and selects Copy link can copy a Ferrite thread link rather than the forge PR address. The menu does not represent the clicked link.
recommendation: Handle the PR badge context gesture and stop propagation after capturing its explicit PR target. Label any thread action Copy thread link. Existing pr-navigation findings own the primary route and visibility behavior; this finding only adds wrong clipboard/context identity.
acceptance: Right-click B's PR while A is focused. Copy PR link returns B's exact forge URL without changing focus. Right-click the remainder of B's row and Copy thread link returns B's Ferrite link. A missing PR URL disables URL actions with a reason.

title: Sidebar and right-panel geometry snap across structural changes
impact: The entire workspace changes width without an intermediate visual state. This directly matches the user's snapping-sidebar complaint.
recommendation: Give sidebar open and close a shared interruptible layout transition. Keep pointer resize immediate, skip restored layouts, retain a closing face until it finishes, and honor reduced motion. Replace the documented prohibition on sidebar motion with the user's requested policy.
acceptance: With motion enabled, record sidebar toggles from toolbar and shortcut. At least one intermediate width must appear, the board must follow without stale hit regions, and reversing before completion must continue from the displayed width. Reduced motion and restored startup layouts must settle immediately.
review_note: Both shell width findings share the explicit snap policy. The detailed report retains separate contracts for collapse, reopen, maximize, and width floors. Panel sizing constraints remain a separate finding.

title: Most panel tab bodies have no transition despite the motion catalog
impact: Tab changes replace large bodies instantly and differ from document previews. The catalog incorrectly promises broader coverage.
recommendation: Give surface activation one transition owner keyed by thread and surface identity. Apply the agreed body transition to Overview, Background, Files, Changes, Terminal, SideChat, Agent and PR, and coordinate document preview fades to avoid double animation. Correct the catalog.
acceptance: Switch through every panel kind and PR subview using both mouse and keyboard. Confirm one visible transition per activation, no replay on unrelated updates, no outgoing input target, and no lost terminal/browser focus.

title: Shelves and connector details reveal their bodies instantly
impact: Expanding a shelf or connector section moves neighboring content without showing the relationship between the header and revealed rows.
recommendation: Add measured, clipped body reveal for nonvirtualized shelves and connector sections. Treat virtualized transcript disclosures separately so visible bounds, scroll anchoring and hit testing agree throughout the transition. Keep chevron timing coordinated with body motion.
acceptance: Expand and collapse every shelf and Connectors, including rapid reversal and a long list. Rows must remain clipped to the displayed body, adjacent headings must move continuously, and reduced motion must reveal the final content immediately.

title: System reduced-motion changes are not observed while Ferrite runs
impact: A user who enables Reduce Motion after launch keeps the previous animation policy until restarting. Turning it off also is not observed.
recommendation: Subscribe to platform accessibility preference changes and route them through set_reduce_motion. Resolve the initial preference before animated content is presented, or adopt a conservative initial state until it is known. Ensure active scroll and layout transitions land when the setting changes.
acceptance: While a loop, panel reveal and smooth scroll are active, toggle the OS preference without restarting. All animation must reach a static state promptly; toggling back must affect subsequent transitions. Repeat with the environment override.

title: Non-macOS builds do not read the system reduced-motion preference
impact: Windows and other supported non-macOS users cannot rely on their system animation preference reaching Ferrite through this integration.
recommendation: Implement the relevant platform setting bridge and change observation on supported operating systems. Preserve the explicit environment override for test and operator control.
acceptance: On each supported non-macOS platform, launch with the system animation setting disabled and then change it while running. Built-in transitions and continuous indicators must follow the setting without an environment variable.

title: Streaming tail follow still jumps with content growth
impact: The answer can move in provider-update increments even though its new text fades in. Send scrolling and jump-to-end already animate, which makes continuous follow inconsistent.
recommendation: Introduce a dedicated interruptible live-follow policy while work is running. Keep idle growth, history restoration and user-driven scroll separate. Preserve the reading anchor and stop following immediately on wheel, scrollbar or page navigation.
acceptance: With a long answer visible at the tail, stream uneven chunks and tool rows. Record intermediate scroll positions, then interrupt with wheel and scrollbar. The transcript must stop exactly where the user takes control and resume only when requested.

title: File discovery silently omits entries beyond fixed limits
impact: Large directories and repositories can contain files that the tree or fuzzy search never exposes, without a truncation notice.
recommendation: Use incremental directory traversal and virtualized rows. If a limit remains, expose it and allow explicit loading or exact-path opening.
acceptance: Use a fixture with 1,100 files in one folder and a target after the 20,000th search entry. The final tree entry and target are reachable, or the UI explicitly provides continuation.

title: Restart restores the Files shell but loses its open files and tool preferences
impact: Operators lose their file working set, selected file, explorer visibility, editor preferences, Changes scope, and review state after restarting.
recommendation: Persist canonical file surfaces, active file, and stable tool preferences. Define separate restoration rules for process resources and unsaved drafts.
acceptance: After restart, restore saved file tabs and active file, chosen tree visibility and wrapping, and the intended review scope. Unsaved drafts must be recovered or safely flushed, never silently lost.

title: Markdown and prose files cannot be edited or navigated to a requested source line in Files
impact: README files, instructions, and text documents open as rendered prose with no source-edit mode. Source links to their line numbers lose their target after redirecting into Files.
recommendation: Separate presentation mode from editability. Preserve line intent and switch to source view for line links, with an explicit render/source toggle.
acceptance: Edit and save README.md and notes.txt. Follow README.md:80 from a conversation and verify source line 80 is visible and highlighted; switching back to rendered view preserves the file.

title: Opening image or document files from the tree bypasses the available preview path
impact: The Files tree tells users that an image is not text instead of showing it. PDFs, audio, video, and document previews also lack the richer in-panel handling available in T3.
recommendation: Unify file opening around file-type dispatch. Reuse Ferrite's image viewer from Files and prioritize PDF, media, and table previews based on actual workflows.
acceptance: Open a PNG from both tree and transcript and reach equivalent image controls. Open a PDF and receive a preview or a specific supported fallback, not a generic text-decoding failure.

title: Disabling diff wrapping clips long lines instead of allowing horizontal scrolling
impact: Long changed expressions become unreadable once wrap is disabled, even though that is the intended mode for comparing code alignment.
recommendation: Use a horizontal scroll container for unwrapped diffs and preserve readable line-number and sign gutters.
acceptance: Put a changed token at column 250, disable wrapping, and scroll to inspect and select that token without resizing the whole window.

title: Hide whitespace changes only removes blank changed lines
impact: Indentation-only and trailing-space changes still dominate reviews when the operator explicitly asks to hide whitespace changes.
recommendation: Compute the diff using an ignore-whitespace option and keep displayed statistics consistent with it.
acceptance: Use separate indentation-only, trailing-space-only, and substantive edits. With the option on, only substantive changes remain; turn it off to restore all changes.

title: Changes stays stale after workspace edits and reviewed marks survive changed contents
impact: The review can show yesterday's loaded content while an agent keeps editing. A reviewed checkmark can remain on a file whose contents changed or whose comparison scope changed.
recommendation: Refresh on a workspace revision signal and associate reviewed state with a diff/content identity. Preserve scroll and folds independently of review validity.
acceptance: Mark a file reviewed, modify it, and return to Changes. Updated hunks appear and the reviewed mark clears. A changed comparison base does not inherit unrelated reviewed marks.

title: Changes lacks full diff navigation and comparison controls present in T3
impact: Large code reviews require more scanning and external tooling. The panel cannot show old and new code side by side, reveal a file through a changes tree, or select a particular completed turn or commit.
recommendation: Build on the existing review core while giving the panel a full diff presentation and explicit scope model. Treat turn history as a separate product decision if checkpoints are not available.
acceptance: Switch stacked/split views, jump to a changed file, read old/new line numbers and syntax, and compare a selected commit or completed turn without leaving the panel. If a capability is deferred, document the supported panel scope.

title: Stage and unstage failures are discarded
impact: A Git lock, permission error, or repository failure makes the stage button appear to do nothing. The operator cannot tell whether the operation ran or what to fix.
recommendation: Return a typed result from staging, display stderr on failure, prevent duplicate in-flight actions, and refresh only with a clear operation outcome.
acceptance: In a disposable repository, create a temporary index lock, click Stage, and see a precise error. Remove the lock and retry successfully. Do the equivalent for Unstage.

title: Terminal surfaces cannot split into simultaneous shells
impact: Running a server and a command side by side requires switching tabs or using an external terminal.
recommendation: Add split groups only if this everyday multitasking workflow is in scope; retain simple single-terminal tabs as the default.
acceptance: Run a server in one split and commands in the other, resize each pane, focus by keyboard, and close one pane without terminating its sibling.

title: Terminal output has no URL or file-path opening flow
impact: Users must copy a localhost URL or compiler file path manually instead of opening the browser or file directly from terminal output.
recommendation: Parse URLs and file locations from terminal text or terminal hyperlink metadata and use the existing browser/file entry points.
acceptance: Print a localhost address, an HTTPS URL, and a relative path with a line number. Open each with the documented gesture and verify the correct destination and line.

title: Panel sizing cannot adapt to narrow layouts or recover a smaller width after wide tools
impact: The panel can consume disproportionate space on a small window. Opening Files or Changes permanently raises the saved width until the operator resizes it, even after returning to Overview.
recommendation: Define narrow-window behavior and preserve a user-chosen compact width separately from temporary tool minimums. Consider a sheet or explicit panel-only mode.
acceptance: At 800, 1,000, and 1,400 pixel window widths, open each tool and return to Overview. All controls remain reachable and chat remains usable; temporary tool expansion does not silently replace the operator's compact width.
review_note: The sticky-width branch is runtime-reproduced: Overview 320px becomes 864px after Files/Changes, auto-hides navigation and remains wide through close/reopen and restart at a 1440px window. Narrow-window/manual-drag branches remain unverified.

title: The main PR affordances bypass the native PR view
impact: The sidebar PR badge and footer PR button open a generic Browser tab, while the Overview PR row and panel menu open the native Summary/Guide/Timeline/Code view. Users can repeatedly choose the obvious PR controls without discovering the built-in review interface.
recommendation: Make the badge and current-PR action open the native PR view by default. Preserve separately named browser and external-browser actions. Do not relabel the existing Open PR in browser command as broken merely because it does what its name says.
acceptance: For the focused thread, the badge and current-PR action show the same native PR tab as Overview and the + menu. Repeated opens leave one native tab. Explicit browser actions still open the browser.
review_note: Focused sidebar badge opened Browser; the Overview PR row opened the real native Summary and Timeline through production reviewr reads. Other PR entry points remain source-only.

title: There is no standalone PR inbox or project-scoped PR browsing destination
impact: Ferrite cannot use the sidebar footer to browse PRs independently of a focused branch. With no known PR on the focused thread, that control does nothing even when the project has other PRs. Reviewers cannot inspect authored, reviewing, or other project PRs through an app-wide list.
recommendation: Add a distinct PR inbox destination with project scope and explicit selection, usable without a focused thread. Keep the current branch shortcut separate. Scope and filter controls should represent actual supported backend queries.
acceptance: From an empty board and a thread without a PR, open Pull requests, select a project, inspect a PR from a different branch, change list scope, and return to the previously selected PR without changing checkout.
review_note: Surface-composition reconciliation corrects prior optional-scope framing: the user explicitly requires an accessible PRs view. A standalone PR browsing destination is required audit repair scope, usable from an empty board or a thread without a current-branch PR. Native forge mutation features remain separate choices. Evidence remains source-proven; no new runtime pass is inferred.

title: The native PR target is the current branch, so links and multiple PRs cannot become independent native tabs
impact: A native tab stores only a number under a thread, and its data loader resolves the current checkout rather than an explicit repository and PR. Ferrite cannot natively open an arbitrary linked PR beside the current PR, retain an older PR after the branch points to a newer one, or navigate a PR comment anchor into the native view.
recommendation: Introduce an explicit selected PR identity containing repository, host, number, and environment or project scope. Read by that target. Retain branch PR discovery as an entry point, then allow independent selected PR tabs and anchor reveals.
acceptance: Open PR 48 and PR 49 from links in the same thread, then switch its branch. Each tab still names and loads its own PR. Equal numbers from different repositories remain distinct. A linked comment or diff anchor reveals the intended content.

title: A known PR without a URL still presents clickable controls that silently do nothing
impact: The accepted PR data shape permits a number and state without a URL. The sidebar still underlines the number and the footer appears enabled, but open_pr returns without feedback. The native PR entry could still work because it needs a number and checkout rather than the missing URL.
recommendation: Use the native PR destination when number and checkout are available. For URL-only actions, apply the same URL availability gate already used by the context menu and palette, with a clear unavailable reason.
acceptance: Render a PR reading with number 415 and url None. Its primary PR control opens native detail or clearly states why unavailable; it never appears as an enabled dead link. Normal production gh usually supplies a URL, so also verify the real failing data before attributing the user's incident to this case.

title: The reported sidebar click failure lacks end-to-end verification at the actual entry points
impact: Existing PR tests establish the internal panel path but do not establish that the reported sidebar click works in the installed app. The source explains nonfocused and missing-URL failures, but the user may also hit a separate native browser or pointer problem when clicking a focused thread.
recommendation: Add an event-level regression test for the real sidebar badge, footer, and + menu. Have the runtime owner exercise the installed app with known URLs on focused and nonfocused threads. Assert destination visibility and selection, not just tab allocation or handler invocation.
acceptance: Record installed build identity, clicked thread, PR URL availability, focused thread, panel active tab before and after, and visible destination. Cover plain and modifier clicks and panel-hidden state. Verify a test fails if the badge handler stops activating its intended destination.

title: Reload discards the last good PR and replaces it with a transient error
impact: A temporary network or authentication failure removes previously readable review context, including access to the Code tab body.
recommendation: Store last-success, pending and error separately. Preserve content on retriable failures and clear it only when authoritative identity or absence changes.
acceptance: Load a PR, simulate a failed refresh, and verify that title, discussion and diff remain visible with an actionable stale/error indicator. Retry succeeds without closing the tab.

title: Authentication and retry guidance do not form a working recovery flow
impact: Users see no PR or a dead-end instruction instead of a recoverable authentication error. Missing CLI, expired credentials and a branch with no PR look identical during discovery.
recommendation: Propagate typed discovery failures to the PR opener and panel. Add a retry button bound to detail reload and make the displayed shortcut match the real binding. Keep host-specific login commands.
acceptance: With a mocked missing executable and then an expired login, show distinct remedies. After restoring authentication, clicking Retry must load the PR. The documented keyboard action must do the same.

title: Rewrite guide displays the oldest matching guide
impact: A rewritten guide can appear not to have changed, and reviewers can read superseded instructions.
recommendation: Select the newest by timestamp or honor the canonical newest-first contract. Add a fixture with multiple guides in real backend order.
acceptance: With older and newer guide comments from a human account, Guide displays the newer one. Rewriting and refreshing must replace it with the latest text.

title: Timeline drops review replies, resolution state and quoted code
impact: Reviewers cannot see answers or distinguish open findings from already resolved or outdated discussions. A finding loses the code context needed to evaluate it.
recommendation: Render complete review threads and their state. Reuse the canonical thread model for Summary, Timeline and inline code comments.
acceptance: A fixture with a resolved, outdated thread and two replies exposes all four facts. The user can open the associated code location and distinguish it from an unresolved thread.

title: Capped PR data is presented as a complete conversation and check result
impact: A reviewer can mistake a partial list for all findings or all checks. Missing failure data can make the summary appear more reassuring than the complete PR.
recommendation: Show explicit partial-data notices separately for checks and discussion. Page remaining data where supported and withhold a complete-pass claim until coverage is known.
acceptance: Inject checks_truncated and comments_truncated independently. Each produces its own notice and route to more data. A truncated success-only subset never claims all checks pass.

title: Checks stop at names and icons without a route to failure details
impact: A failed job requires manually finding the run on the forge. Users cannot inspect the result from the displayed check or distinguish some important status categories.
recommendation: Carry check URLs and useful status distinctions through the model. Add a Details action with visible open failure handling.
acceptance: A failed job opens its own run page from the PR panel. Cancelled and approval-required runs have distinct labels and appropriate next actions.

title: Descriptions, comments and guides render as raw text
impact: PR templates, code fences, tables, checklists, image evidence and linked documents lose their intended presentation and interaction.
recommendation: Use a shared Markdown component with forge-relative links, image handling, code copy and safe task-list interaction.
acceptance: An example PR with a linked issue, fenced code, table, checklist and image renders each correctly. Links open their actual destinations and long code remains usable.

title: No native comment, reply, review verdict or resolution workflow
impact: Users must leave the PR pane or ask an agent to conduct the review. They cannot prepare a batch of inline comments and submit an approval or request changes in the UI.
recommendation: Add typed, permission-aware native review operations or explicitly label the limited workflow and provide reliable forge handoff. Keep failed review drafts.
acceptance: Compose an inline comment and approval, fail the submit once, retry without losing text, then see the posted review. Reply and resolve a thread and verify the new state after refresh.

title: PR metadata cannot be edited or managed in the native panel
impact: Users cannot correct a title or description, request reviewers, or apply labels while reviewing in Ferrite.
recommendation: Extend the domain model and add focused editors with explicit saving/error states and permission checks.
acceptance: Edit title/body and change labels/review requests without leaving the panel. A rejected save retains the draft and shows the reason.

title: Agent-backed PR operations have no panel-level pending, success or failure lifecycle
impact: Clicking Merge, Ready, Write guide or Create PR can appear to do nothing while work queues behind another turn. Repeated clicks can enqueue repeated requests.
recommendation: Keep agent execution if desired, but model an operation with a target, state and result. Show that state beside the initiating control and deduplicate repeated requests.
acceptance: Click an action while a turn is busy. Show Queued and the target PR, block duplicate enqueue, then transition through Running to success/failure and refresh the affected data.

title: Lifecycle actions lack inverse operations and branch maintenance
impact: A user can enable auto-merge or close a PR but cannot undo those choices from the same UI. Updating a stale branch and approving blocked workflows also require leaving the panel.
recommendation: Model the current settings and complete reversible lifecycle actions. Gate them by actual host capability and permission.
acceptance: Enable then disable auto-merge, close then reopen a PR, toggle maintainer edits both ways, and update an eligible branch. Each result appears after refresh.

title: PR action prompts lose canonical host and repository identity
impact: For forks, multiple remotes, enterprise hosts or non-GitHub forges, the agent must reconstruct the target and may fail or act in the wrong repository. No wrong-target mutation was performed in this audit.
recommendation: Carry an explicit target identity through every operation. For agent handoffs, include the URL and provider-specific command plus a target-verification step. Resolve branch deletion from the PR head repository.
acceptance: With origin=fork and upstream=base, generated operations target the named PR and correct remote branch. GitLab/Azure reads generate matching provider operations or clearly unavailable controls.

title: Concurrent PR reads can land out of order and retire the current tab
impact: A slow old response can overwrite newer details, or remove the tab for the PR now on the branch. The source permits this race; timing was not reproduced.
recommendation: Capture canonical target and request generation, deduplicate pending reads, and reject stale completions before they modify cache or surfaces.
acceptance: Delay read A, start read B for a different current PR, complete B then A. B stays visible and its tab remains. Repeated open of one pending PR creates one request.

title: PR read workers have no effective cancellation or deadline
impact: A hung forge process can leave Reading visible indefinitely and retain a worker after the pane is closed. Repeated forced opens can accumulate stuck reads.
recommendation: Thread cancellation and a deadline through the one-shot adapter; cancel on supersession and release the process tree. Share equivalent safeguards with badge discovery.
acceptance: A fake gh that never exits reaches a visible timeout. Closing or superseding the request terminates its process tree, and repeated retries do not leave worker processes behind.

title: Review verdicts and empty-body approvals are absent from the snapshot
impact: Reviewers cannot tell who approved, requested changes, or had a review dismissed. An approval with no written body disappears entirely.
recommendation: Preserve structured review outcomes, including empty-body verdicts and whether the review applies to the latest head.
acceptance: An approval with an empty body appears with author and verdict. A later push marks an old review appropriately. Changes requested and dismissed reviews remain distinguishable.

title: PR panel omits the checkout-versus-host sync warning
impact: Users may confuse local changes shown in Code with what reviewers can actually see on the host, because the PR view drops the unpushed/behind warning.
recommendation: Restore the sync notice and explicitly identify which revision Code displays. Prefer the hosted PR revisions for hosted review operations.
acceptance: With two unpushed commits, the PR panel says so and identifies the displayed code revision. With a behind checkout, it does not silently present the local diff as the current hosted PR.

title: Guide is a comment convention without revision-aware review workflow
impact: A guide can remain apparently current after a push, and its file references cannot act as a structured review tour. Guide generation has no local run or failure state.
recommendation: Decide whether a comment guide is an intentional reduced feature. At minimum record head identity, generation state and stale status. Full parity needs ordered stops with linked excerpts.
acceptance: After generating a guide, push a new commit. The guide is visibly stale. A failed rewrite retains the old guide and offers retry; successful stops open the corresponding file and lines.

title: Merge controls ignore permissions, allowed methods and readiness
impact: The panel offers actions the user cannot perform and always presents Merge on an open PR, even with conflicts or blocked checks. The user cannot choose a supported merge method.
recommendation: Fetch viewer permissions, available merge methods and readiness. Disable or relabel unavailable actions, let users select a method, and bind confirmation to the intended target/revision.
