acceptance: For a read-only viewer there is no enabled Merge. A conflicting PR displays the blocker. A squash-only repository offers the correct method and the operation reports its actual result.

title: Reopen failures produce a log entry without a visible error
impact: A parked thread can appear unresponsive when its stored history cannot be loaded. The search also clears before the failure, removing the user's recovery context.
recommendation: Return a visible per-thread recovery message and retain the row and query on failure. Let Undo report failed restores instead of consuming its notice silently.
acceptance: With a controlled unreadable or missing thread log, click the parked row, invoke Reopen last, and undo Park. Each path identifies the failed thread, shows the failure, and leaves a retryable state.

title: Undo Park does not restore group membership or a dissolved group
impact: Undo restores a transcript but cannot restore the grouped workspace that Park changed. Users can lose their arrangement after what appears to be a reversible action.
recommendation: Capture the group and placement before parking, then restore surviving membership and layout on Undo. Report conflicts when concurrent edits prevent exact restoration.
acceptance: Create a two-thread group, park one member, then Undo. Both threads must return to the original group and arrangement. Repeat with multi-selection and a larger group.

title: Bulk Park discards individual failures and clears the selection
impact: A mixed success/failure batch reports only Parked. The operator cannot tell which requested parks failed without inspecting the remaining list.
recommendation: Collect a result for every requested thread. Show the successful and failed counts, retain failures in the selection, and offer Undo only for the successful subset.
acceptance: Force one of three selected threads to refuse Park. The UI says two parked and names the failure. The failing thread stays selected. Undo restores only the two successful parks.

title: Sidebar search matches titles only
impact: A thread cannot be found from its branch, PR number, or remembered message text through the sidebar search, even though the result row itself displays a PR number.
recommendation: Extend a shared thread-search model to branch and PR metadata, then add cancellable content search with snippets and navigation to the matched message. Keep the current project scope explicit.
acceptance: Search a unique branch, a PR number, and text found only inside a parked transcript. Each query returns the correct thread. A content result opens at the matching message.

title: Keyboard search navigation does not reveal the highlighted result
impact: Arrow-key navigation can move the highlighted search result beyond the viewport while the keyboard remains in the search field. Enter then opens an unseen row.
recommendation: Give search results the same explicit reveal behavior as ordinary nav rows. Reveal on query reset and every highlight change without moving keyboard focus out of the field.
acceptance: Populate enough matching threads to exceed the viewport. Press Down to the final result and Up to the first. Each highlighted row must remain visible throughout.
review_note: Opening a broad search after sidebar scrolling retained the old scroll offset with cursor reset to result 0. Visible rows began at 09, but Enter opened the invisible selected result 02. A separate visible-result Down/Enter path worked. Live reordering remains untested.

title: Live search results can change the Enter target or make Enter a no-op
impact: A background status change can reorder the results under the user's highlight. A result disappearing can leave a visibly selected row that Enter will not open.
recommendation: Store the selected ThreadId and resolve its current index. Use one resolved selection for drawing and activation. Pick a documented fallback when that thread disappears.
acceptance: Highlight a search result, then cause another matching thread to move between Active and Working. Enter must still open the highlighted identity. Remove the selected final result and confirm the visible fallback opens.

title: Project scope has no search, multi-project selection, or persistence
impact: Large project lists require manual scanning. Users cannot watch a chosen subset of projects together, and the chosen project scope is lost on a new view.
recommendation: Use a searchable scope picker with explicit All and selected-project states. Persist the selection if the product intends it to survive restart. Multi-project scope should remain optional.
acceptance: With 30 projects, type a project name into the filter, select two projects, and see only their threads. Reopen the application and confirm the selected scope is restored.

title: Opening a thread outside the project filter leaves its sidebar selection hidden
impact: The main view can show a thread with no selected row in the nav. This weakens the orientation promise that selection follows the shown thread.
recommendation: On explicit cross-project navigation, reveal the destination by widening the filter or drawing a clearly labeled current-thread exception. Preserve the user's scope on background updates.
acceptance: Filter to project A, then open a thread in B through history or the palette. The destination has a visible selected nav row or an explicit outside-filter indicator. Background updates alone must not change the scope.

title: Pinned rows cannot be reordered directly
impact: Users cannot arrange persistent pinned priorities by dragging. Unpinning and repinning moves only to the end, which is a cumbersome ordering substitute.
recommendation: Add an explicit reorder destination for pinned rows and persist the resulting order. Preserve the existing drag-to-board behavior by distinguishing its destination.
acceptance: Pin three threads, drag the final one to the first slot, restart, and see the same order. Dragging into the board must still use the established grouping behavior.

title: Multi-selection applies only to Park and is absent from slim rows
impact: The UI suggests a multi-thread selection model but Snooze, Mark unread, Unpin and Delete still act on one context-menu thread. Parked and Snoozed rows cannot join that selection with the same gesture.
recommendation: Make the supported batch operations explicit and label them with their target count. Apply the selection model consistently to applicable shelves. Do not imply a batch for actions that remain singular.
acceptance: Select three rows and invoke each supported batch action. Its label names all three targets and its outcome accounts for each. Cmd-click on a Snoozed or Parked row follows the same documented selection behavior.

title: Project editing and removal lack a contextual navigation entry point
impact: After the project tree retired, users must discover the command palette to rename a project, manage its directories, or remove it. These capabilities exist but the normal project filter does not lead to them.
recommendation: Add Edit project to the selected project's filter entry or to the thread context menu. Reuse the existing editor and its validation.
acceptance: Starting with a visible thread, reach its project editor with the pointer, rename the project, and manage its directories without opening the command palette.

title: New thread on the same branch or worktree requires manual reselection
impact: Starting another conversation about the same checkout takes an extra workspace-selection step and can accidentally aim work at the main checkout if the user assumes the contextual action preserves the branch.
recommendation: Offer an explicit New thread in this checkout action that carries the thread's workspace binding. Keep the existing project-level action accurately named.
acceptance: From a thread in a non-main worktree, choose New thread in this checkout. The draft names the identical path and branch before send, and the new session starts there.

title: Park combines session closure and sidebar settlement, unlike T3
impact: Ferrite has no separate lightweight settled state or inactivity-based settlement control. Tidying a running thread by parking ends its session and can remove group membership. T3 users may expect settlement to be a list-placement action distinct from archive.
recommendation: Decide explicitly whether Park remains a session-lifecycle operation. If parity is wanted, add a separate settled placement and auto-settle policy. Explain the session effect before treating Park as the equivalent of T3 Settle.
acceptance: Document and exercise Settle or Park during a running turn, while grouped, after inactivity and after merge. The observed session and membership behavior must match the labels and chosen product policy.

title: Provider version checks and updates target local binaries while a remote server is active
impact: A user trying to repair a remote CLI sees the local CLI version and can update the local installation. Ferrite then tells the remote server that its CLI was replaced, causing unnecessary remote session retirement without upgrading that remote CLI.
recommendation: Route remote provider inspection and upgrades through the selected server, with machine-labelled progress. If remote upgrades remain unsupported, label local controls and never invalidate remote sessions after a local update.
acceptance: Use fake local and remote provider executables with distinct versions and update markers. In a remote window, update the selected remote provider and verify only its marker changes and only its sessions retire. A local-only fallback must name this computer and leave remote sessions intact.

title: Provider setup stops at CLI presence and update status
impact: A new user or a user with expired credentials cannot complete provider setup, identify the active account, or retry provider sign-in from Ferrite settings. Existing native CLI authentication can still work.
recommendation: Add a compact provider readiness/setup panel with the correct machine, detected binary, version, account/auth status where supported, setup instructions or managed install, recheck, and sign-in/retry actions. Preserve externally managed CLI installs.
acceptance: Exercise absent CLI, signed-out CLI, expired auth, supported logged-in CLI and CLI version rejection. Each state has a distinct message and working next action. Rechecking reflects changed credentials without starting a paid prompt. Account switching must not leave existing helpers using the old credential binding.

title: An unavailable native conversation has no same-thread context recovery path
impact: If a provider's saved conversation disappears or cannot be resumed, the Ferrite transcript can remain readable while sending another prompt repeats the same failed resume. Users must reconstruct the conversation or switch providers through a separate workflow.
recommendation: Classify resume errors, preserve the failed prompt, and provide an explicit fresh-conversation recovery action with a context preview or clear disclosure. Keep provider-lock contention as a refusal.
acceptance: With a provider stub that rejects the old native id, recover within the same Ferrite thread and send the preserved prompt once to a new native id with retained context. The old transcript remains. A thread-in-use refusal must not silently fork. Live-provider behavior remains to be checked.

title: Provider choices do not include T3's additional drivers or named provider instances
impact: Users of Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, Antigravity, Kiro, Muse, Pi, FX or registry ACP agents cannot select those drivers in Ferrite. Users cannot configure separate named instances of one driver with different credentials, environments or binaries.
recommendation: Decide which additional providers the product actually wants before expanding. If multiple configurations matter first, introduce instance identity separately from driver kind and retain per-driver capability gates.
acceptance: For any adopted driver, complete setup, new thread, stream, approval, stop, reopen and failure recovery. For instances, run two named configurations concurrently, restart Ferrite and verify each resumes with its original config. Do not mark an icon or model-list entry as support.

title: Claude Auto and Don't ask are available per session but absent from new-thread defaults
impact: An operator who consistently uses Claude Auto or Don't ask must change each new thread or edit JSON/native CLI configuration. Settings cannot express all permission modes that Ferrite already supports.
recommendation: Build defaults from a provider-specific launch-mode catalog that includes supported Auto and Don't ask, while retaining live-only restrictions for mode changes and a visible representation for unknown saved values.
acceptance: Select Auto in Settings through the UI, relaunch and create a Claude thread. The provider receives auto and the setting remains selected. Repeat for dontAsk and a previously saved unsupported value. This is an internal Ferrite inconsistency; T3's unified modes are only a related comparison.

title: Provider defaults have no project override or fallback-model settings
impact: Users who work across projects with different model/permission needs must keep changing thread choices or global defaults. A chosen default provider exhausting its allowance does not have a configured fallback model for new threads.
recommendation: Prioritize project defaults only if repeated manual changes are a real workflow. Use a small inheritance model and show the resolved source. Treat allowance-triggered fallback as a separate opt-in policy.
acceptance: Configure two projects with different defaults, create a thread in each and verify the right provider/model/permission after restart. Existing threads retain their own choices. A synthetic exhausted allowance selects only the configured fallback for new threads and visibly explains that selection.

title: Remote access supports SSH, not T3's pairing links and alternate routes
impact: A machine reachable through a T3 pairing URL or relay cannot be added through Ferrite's machine settings. Ferrite also expects ferrited to be installed on the remote PATH before connection.
recommendation: Do not describe remote support as absent. Document the existing SSH prerequisite and decide whether pairing/relay or assisted bootstrap is needed. Keep these optional expansions separate from the real remote settings/update defects.
acceptance: For present scope, a configured SSH target reconnects and names an absent daemon clearly. If alternate routes are added, pair once, force direct-route failure and verify failover preserves machine/thread identity and requires no duplicate environment.

title: Empty browser address entry lacks a clear editable-region affordance
impact: The empty location row reads as navigation icons, a static Address label, blank space and a separate arrow. The editable region has no prompt; the label and annotation control also spend address width.
recommendation: Design one location control with explicit empty, idle, hover, focus, editing, loading and invalid states while preserving useful one-line address space.
acceptance: An empty tab clearly indicates where to enter a URL before interaction. Hover and keyboard focus identify the field; text and navigation remain usable at supported widths. Verify these native states individually.
review_note: Only empty presentation is directly observed here. Native hover/focus/narrow-width behavior remains unverified. T3 also uses a transparent idle field, so absence of a permanent border is not itself the defect.

title: Native PR read errors run beyond the panel and hide their cause and recovery text
impact: A long PR read error is centered on one unwrapped line wider than the panel. Its beginning and recovery instruction are clipped, leaving the operator unable to read the failure.
recommendation: Render read failures in a width-constrained, wrapping body with a visible relevant recovery action. Preserve the current PR identity and useful previous content.
acceptance: Force a long read error at ordinary/minimum panel widths. The full cause and next action remain readable and reachable; retry recovers without losing target identity.
review_note: Parent inspected the screenshot and the centered pr_note render path. The nonexistent synthetic repository caused this expected read error; it is not evidence that normal repositories fail.

title: Thread context lacks an independent compact details surface
impact: Thread context lives in Overview inside the full tabbed workspace panel, so checking it competes with Browser, Files, PR and other tools. Existing context controls do not provide a separate lightweight card alongside the active tool. This is distinct from remembered-width corruption.
recommendation: Provide independently accessible lightweight thread details, with separate visibility and responsive popover behavior, while preserving the active full tool surface and conversation reading space. Link agents to their main child conversations and Git/PR actions to explicit full-tool targets.
acceptance: Keep Browser, Files or PR open while showing and dismissing thread details. Pointer and Command-Shift-B target only details; Escape returns focus without closing the tool. Exercise narrow-size fallback, overflow, Find clearance, thread identity, live status, meaningful motion and reduced motion.
review_note: The inventory source links use the pinned newer comparison checkout. reports/thread-details-card-correction.md separately cites the exact installed revision and records native T3 identity, toggle, shortcut, one responsive mode transition, empty-workspace coexistence and Escape checks. Those T3 successes do not upgrade this Ferrite composition gap to runtime-reproduced. This finding was omitted from the earlier 176-record tally.

title: Quote previews hide their full contents with no disclosure
impact: The user cannot inspect the whole passage they are about to cite, and a sent prompt cannot reveal the complete quote or a preloaded long comment. Similar openings become indistinguishable.
recommendation: Use a text-sized citation row or chip with full inspection and comment editing. Preserve compactness through disclosure rather than irreversible clipping. Restore provenance under transcript-006; this finding separately covers local readability even when a source is unavailable.
acceptance: A 5,000-character citation, two citations with identical opening words, a code excerpt and a multiline comment can each be inspected in full before and after send. The UI clearly distinguishes source text from comment text at narrow pane widths. Screenshot review confirms readable wrapping and controls.
review_note: A roughly 991-character response attached as context was truncated in the 88px tile and could not be inspected by clicking it. Full prose/code still reached the provider. This does not test the >10,000-character attachment limit.

title: The Cite toolbar is pointer-only and does not observe keyboard selection
impact: A keyboard user cannot reach or activate the displayed Cite action. A selection changed without mouse release does not create a fresh offer.
recommendation: Give Cite a focusable native control and explicit keyboard activation while retaining a captured selection until activation settles. Observe selection changes independently of mouse-up. Keep Escape dismissal and the oversize explanation.
acceptance: Select a passage, Tab to Cite, activate with Enter and with Space, and confirm exactly one citation and no message send. Keyboard-only selection exposes the same action. Escape restores a predictable focus target without interrupting the agent.

title: Attach message as context silently does nothing for long messages
impact: The visible attach action can produce no attachment, error or explanation for a long assistant answer. This is a concrete no-op that can resemble the reported citation regression.
recommendation: Use a whole-message source reference, or show a disabled reason and offer a shorter selected passage. A successful-looking action must not disappear silently.
acceptance: Exercise 1, 2, 10,000 and 10,001 trimmed characters through the actual menu. Each action either creates context or displays an explicit reason. Unicode bounds match the explanation.

title: Ordinary blockquote text is reclassified as an uneditable citation on restore
impact: An ordinary prompt can change into attachment cards when reopened or recalled. Its text leaves the main editor, and its editing affordances disappear. This is a structure and editability defect; the words usually remain serialized.
recommendation: Persist typed citation records or an unambiguous versioned encoding. Keep literal Markdown literal. Preserve multiline comments and support legacy prompt decoding without treating every new leading blockquote as structured context.
acceptance: Round-trip literal leading blockquotes, nested quotes, the literal ↩ marker, blank lines, Unicode and deliberate citations through draft restart, history and resend. Compare both text and editable record types. General text remains in the general editor.

title: A quote-only prompt renders differently when a file is attached
impact: Adding an unrelated file can turn the citation into raw > text in the sent prompt. Draft restoration reconstructs the quote differently from transcript rendering. Imported comments can also absorb the attachment trailer and hide the file preview.
recommendation: Decode a prompt once into text, quotes, files and annotations, then render that result. Do not repeatedly split and recompose transport syntax inside render helpers.
acceptance: Test the cross-product of zero or nonempty main text, one or several quotes, zero or multiline comments, file/image attachments and browser annotations. Sent, reopened and recalled forms retain the same quote rows, file previews and comment boundaries. No transport token appears as comment prose.

title: Valid image attachments can show a permanent false Failed tile
impact: An image supported by the rendering library can appear broken before it is decoded. A repaired or newly created file can remain Failed until the app process restarts.
recommendation: Let the supported decoder determine displayability. Use a neutral dimension fallback while metadata is unknown. Key cached facts by a file version or explicit attachment identity and expose a retry after changes. This is separate from composer-07's provider readiness problem.
acceptance: Valid SVG, AVIF, TIFF, PNG and a JPEG with large metadata each show a preview or an accurate format-specific explanation. A missing/corrupt file repaired at the same path recovers without restarting. Replacing an image updates dimensions and caption.

title: Draft file previews and sent image previews lack keyboard activation
impact: A keyboard user can remove a draft file but cannot activate its preview. Image preview is keyboard-capable in the draft, then loses that capability after the message sends.
recommendation: Share a semantic preview control between draft and transcript renderers, with a stable accessible name and focus restoration when preview closes. Keep removal a separate control.
acceptance: Open and close text and image previews entirely by keyboard before and after send. Every activation opens once without sending a message. Tab exposes preview and remove as distinct labeled actions. An accessibility inspection sees buttons rather than anonymous clickable text.

title: Attachment history stores mutable paths rather than retained content
impact: Retry and history can refer to changed or deleted file content. A pasted screenshot depends on a temporary file even after its prompt has been saved. The visual record is not a reliable record of the bytes originally sent. ADR 0004 explicitly chooses path storage, so this is a documented product tradeoff with incomplete user feedback, not an accidental omission of a promised byte store.
recommendation: Distinguish live file references from retained attachments. Copy clipboard media and explicit attachment snapshots into an owned durable store and keep content identity with history. Detect stale references and expose reattach/retry instead of silently changing content. Keep workspace @mentions live if that is the intended contract.
acceptance: Send version A of a fixture, replace the original with B, reopen and inspect history, then retry. The UI and provider payload agree on A versus B and never silently substitute. A pasted screenshot survives restart and routine temp cleanup, or displays an actionable missing-asset state before send.

title: The attachment shelf has no bounded overflow policy
impact: At narrow pane widths, many attachments can consume the available conversation height. Source shows unbounded growth; the installed app must establish the exact clipping or displacement symptom.
recommendation: Measure the installed layout with many attachments, then provide a bounded attachment region or compact summary with explicit expansion. Preserve navigation, removal and the active editor. Do not copy T3's expanded wrapping blindly; its resting summary and screenshot horizontal scrolling are the relevant comparison.
acceptance: At 360 pixel pane width and 600 pixel window height, add 12 images, six citations and long-named files. The editor, Send and all attachments remain reachable by pointer and keyboard. Resize and remove items without losing focus or the visible edit position. Capture before/after screenshots.

title: Scrollbar navigation does not consistently take ownership from automatic scrolling
impact: Track clicks during a send/latest ease can be overwritten by the next animation frame. Thumb movement after the ease can leave the sent-prompt anchor active, allowing the first tool event to snap back to the tail if runway remains. Extends the motion report's interruption inventory; does not duplicate motion-008.
recommendation: Emit a common reader-navigation transition from both scrollbar track clicks and thumb movement, independently of whether a tween exists. Cancel pending send anchoring before applying the user offset; preserve explicit drag-to-end reattachment.
acceptance: Real track clicks and pointer drags interrupt movement at every tween phase. Repeat a short thumb drag after send settlement with runway remaining, then emit the first tool event. The chosen passage stays put after later frames/events; dragging to the bottom still resumes follow.

title: Scrollbar track clicks use the wrong scroll distance
impact: Track clicks overshoot the position corresponding to the painted thumb and clamp to the end early because the click branch multiplies by content height instead of content height minus viewport height.
recommendation: Share one inverse coordinate conversion across thumb painting, dragging and track clicks. Handle insets and minimum thumb size explicitly, or define an intentional page-by-page track policy.
acceptance: For fixed content and viewport sizes, clicking 25%, 50% and 75% of effective thumb travel centers the thumb at the clicked position within a specified tolerance. Repeat with minimum-size and horizontal thumbs. The 2000px content/500px viewport/0.5 fraction arithmetic yields 750px of scroll, not 1000px.

title: The latest button undercounts hidden content when send runway remains
impact: The latest button and lower fade can be absent while real answer lines remain below the viewport. rows_below subtracts normal padding and synthetic runway from a native maximum that already excludes padding.
recommendation: Separate real content-end distance from padded scrollable-end distance, and audit consumers against the native list's actual treatment of padding and unmeasured heights.
acceptance: With at least 200px of runway, position more than two lines of real content below the viewport. After the configured delay, the latest button and bottom fade are present. Latest removes the runway and reaches the final row. Repeat with no runway and with unmeasured rows.

title: Expanding finished work at the tail does not preserve the clicked heading
impact: A completed fold or large tool detail expands while native tail follow remains enabled, moving the heading upward and possibly out of view. This concerns viewport ownership, distinct from motion.md inventory row 37 body animation and transcript-004 nested group height caps.
recommendation: Capture the clicked disclosure's anchor before changing rows, cancel prior positioning, and reveal new content after measurement while retaining the heading. Define the working-turn follow exception explicitly.
acceptance: At an idle tail, opening and closing a fold hiding several viewports leaves its heading at the same screen position. Repeat a long tool detail near the composer, expansion during a latest jump, rapid reversal, and a separately specified live-streaming case.

title: Keyboard End retains the send spacer that the latest button removes
impact: End can retain a large blank area below the newest message; during runway sizing a later layout callback can reassert the prompt position. The latest button clears this state, so explicit return-to-end actions disagree.
recommendation: Route every explicit return-to-end action through one state transition that releases send anchoring, pending runway placement and synthetic space before landing. Let the caller choose timing separately.
acceptance: End and the latest pill from identical send states leave zero runway, the same final-row inset, and active following. End during the first sizing frame is not overwritten by a later runway callback. Repeat with reduced motion.

title: Find can compete with an existing jump or live follow inside a visible row
impact: Opening Find does not cancel follow/ease. Revealing a match only cancels when its entire row is offscreen; a tall intersecting row can let the old tween or stream move away from the result. Distinct from transcript-001 hidden-content search coverage.
recommendation: Treat Find navigation as a viewport-ownership transition regardless of whole-row visibility. Scope later reveal callbacks to the search request and transcript generation, and let manual navigation cancel them.
acceptance: Find a result in a tall row halfway through a latest jump. The occurrence remains visible after the old tween would have ended and after later text/tool events. Repeat for a match already visible while following. Manual navigation after searching must win over delayed reveal corrections.

title: Width changes lack a reading anchor inside a tall row
impact: A right-panel toggle or resize can change which sentence is visible when the viewport lies entirely inside a long answer. Ferrite saves only a fully visible row start and otherwise retains a numeric pixel offset through rewrapping. Displacement is inferred and needs runtime measurement; T3 sentence-level preservation is also unverified.
recommendation: Preserve a text/sub-row anchor for tall content, while retaining row-inset anchoring when sufficient. Specify the fallback for content without a text anchor and verify both implementations before claiming parity superiority.
acceptance: A distinctive sentence in a multi-viewport answer remains at a documented readable inset across panel open/close/maximize/restore and width changes. Repeat with a code fence and a visible row boundary. Confirm on the installed build before labeling it runtime-reproduced.

title: Saved jump, runway and resize indices are not rebased when rows change
impact: Pending movement can use an obsolete numeric row index after disclosure changes, retention or history replacement. Native logical top is rebased, but EaseTarget::Row, Runway.index and resize_anchor are separate and are not rebased/reset together. The omission is source-proven; a wrong-row landing remains an inferred concurrent-transition outcome.
recommendation: Store semantic RowId plus transcript generation for pending targets, resolve after each projection, and cancel missing targets. Reset or deliberately translate all geometry state on history replacement.
acceptance: Insert/remove rows before a moving send target and verify it still lands on the same prompt ID. Repeat with width reflow, retention, target removal and generation replacement. Returning from another thread never revives a command against a different history generation.

title: Page navigation does not subtract the pinned prompt's covered area
impact: Page movement uses full viewport height minus one line even though the pinned prompt obscures the top. When the mask exceeds that line, content can be hidden on both adjacent pages. Existing keyboard tests verify offsets and follow state, not readable coverage.
recommendation: Compute page travel from the unobscured viewport using the measured top mask, and retain a readable overlap. Define the transition when the pinned prompt changes height.
acceptance: Page up/down through numbered answer lines under a two-line pinned prompt. Every line must appear unobscured and adjacent pages overlap. Repeat with a short prompt, no pinned prompt, and changing prompt height.

title: Opening an evicted agent through its transcript row never requests saved history
impact: A real agent can open as an empty transcript despite its history existing in Ferrite storage.
recommendation: Make the Panel agent opener request and observe saved history, render loading/error/coverage states, and support retry through the same loader as full-Pane navigation.
acceptance: With a small child-retention limit, finish and evict agent A, then click A in Main. Its stored prompt and response load without resuming its provider. A failing read shows a visible retry that succeeds after the storage failure clears.
review_note: The defect requires an unretained child. The default retains 128 children. The source condition is established, but its frequency and the installed restart path were not reproduced.

title: Agent Panel views omit coverage, decision guidance and full status
impact: A partial, waiting, failed, or unavailable child can look like an ordinary read-only transcript with no explanation of what the operator should do.
recommendation: Give the primary agent drill an identity/status header, coverage explanation, and an explicit route to its pending request. Preserve read-only prompting semantics. State whether Stop targets this child.
acceptance: Open agents in Pending, Waiting, Failed, NotLoaded, Partial, and ToolActivity states. Each view states its true status/coverage. Waiting exposes a route to the exact request; opening and answering it preserves the parent draft.

title: Generic thread opening can replace Main with the first pending child
impact: A user selecting a thread can unexpectedly land in a background agent and lose the visible Main composer, while a direct agent-row click instead opens a side tab.
recommendation: Separate Open thread from Open request, and visibly name child destinations on request actions. Use one explicit inspection/follow policy; do not silently retarget generic thread opening to whichever decision happens to be first.
acceptance: With Main and two children awaiting different approvals, activate the generic thread card, then each exact request. The generic action opens Main; request actions name and open the selected owner. Back returns to the prior place and Main draft remains unchanged.

title: Background Stop never clears its pending marker or offers retry after failure
impact: A rejected or ineffective stop can leave Stopping... permanently disabled. Reused task IDs can inherit this state across threads or session generations.
recommendation: Key stop requests by thread, session generation and task; clear on failure/completion, expose failures beside Stop, and allow retry if the provider does not settle.
acceptance: Reject a Stop request. Its error appears beside the background line and Stop becomes enabled again. Reuse the same native task ID in another thread and a later session and confirm no inherited pending marker.

title: Background-work Stop excludes every subagent it counts
impact: A mixed commands-and-agents line offers Stop but stops only commands; an agents-only line has no Stop even where child interruption is supported.
recommendation: Make Stop scope explicit and use the existing child-stop operation for stoppable child work. If one action cannot stop everything, give per-item controls and name the remaining work.
acceptance: Run one command and one stoppable child after Main settles. Stop either stops both, or clearly says Stop commands and leaves a named child Stop control. An agents-only state offers child Stop where supported.

title: Background task views disagree about which work exists
impact: The transcript can say Waiting on a subagent while the Background tab is empty; users must learn three different background-work views.
recommendation: Use one attributed work inventory for the transcript summary, detail dialog and Background tab. Include agents and shell tasks, retain owner identity, and distinguish awaited work from work merely running. Make palette naming identify the destination.
acceptance: With an agents-only workload, the transcript count, Details and Background tab show the same agent. With a command known only from a progress snapshot, every view includes it. A dev server running after Main completes reads Running unless the provider says it is awaited.
review_note: Clicking an agent name opened its updated child transcript, but that same row’s View live output opened Background with No output yet. This is a reproduced branch of the inconsistent work/output model; other inventory branches retain source-only status.

title: Agent inspection tabs disappear on restart despite the Panel persistence contract
impact: A user returning to a long review loses the agent inspection tabs and can land on a surviving Background tab instead.
recommendation: Persist stable agent identities and reconstruct saved drills lazily, or make this exception an explicit product decision with a clear recoverable list of recent agents. Preserve deliberate active-tab choice when an ephemeral tab cannot restore.
acceptance: Open Overview, Background and Agent A with A active, restart, and verify A restores with saved history or an explicit recovery state. The application does not silently show Background as if the user chose it.

title: Find cannot discover text hidden by turn or tool disclosures
impact: A reader can receive zero matches for text that exists in the loaded conversation. The new default turn folding makes this common for intermediate explanations and command output.
recommendation: Build a search index from semantic messages and tool details. Keep visible-content selection separate. Map each hit to the disclosure chain and stable content identity.
acceptance: A token present only in a collapsed intermediate answer or collapsed command result is counted before expansion. Next match opens the required disclosures and reveals the exact occurrence. Closing Find preserves the reader's place.
review_note: Find reported no matches for text inside a folded Read call; after disclosure it returned 1/1 for a unique final-passage phrase. Closed-turn search remains source-only. The separate screenshot-only paging blankness is inconclusive because headless repaint omitted unrelated shell regions.

title: Long transcript retention has no equivalent of earlier-turn paging
impact: Readers of long sessions cannot reliably return to the earliest prompts or search them from the transcript. Stored events may still exist; this is a navigation and retrieval limitation, not a claim of data loss.
recommendation: Add a stored-history cursor and older-page loading to the main transcript. Preserve bounded memory with a sliding window. Show partial coverage rather than silently presenting the retained start as the conversation start.
acceptance: A fixture larger than both retention budgets can reach its original prompt through an earlier-history control. Prepending a page does not move the current visible sentence. A failed page load shows a retry action. Confirm the installed build before promoting this inferred gap to a reproduced defect.

title: Successful turns erase the visible plan history
impact: Readers cannot check which planned steps were completed or left pending after a successful answer. Expanding Worked does not recover the checklist.
recommendation: Snapshot the last checklist state per turn and render it as historical work. Retain the useful blocked presentation for interrupted turns, with no live spinner after settlement.
acceptance: After a successful turn ends, expand Worked and inspect the original ordered steps and their final statuses. A pending step remains visibly pending. The same historical plan survives reopening the thread.

title: Opening one tool removes the entire work-group height cap
impact: Inspecting one result in a large group can expand all its compact rows into the main transcript and displace surrounding content far beyond the intended bounded work list.
recommendation: Retain the base cap of min(288 px, half the viewport) and add measured detail height. Keep the group's scroll anchor when children open and close.
acceptance: With 100 compact calls, opening a two-line result grows the group only by that result's added height. The other compact calls remain internally scrollable. Closing the child restores the previous group position.

title: Citations and copied text do not retain a navigable source message
impact: A cited passage reaches the model, but the reader cannot jump back to the original answer or copy a stable link to a specific prompt. Repeated text makes manual relocation ambiguous.
recommendation: Add optional structured provenance to Reply without breaking plain-text provider prompts. Add a prompt/message deep link and a source-opening action on sent citation chips.
acceptance: A citation made from a folded historical response opens the exact original passage after reopening the thread. A copied prompt link lands on that prompt. Duplicate passages resolve by message identity, not substring alone.

title: Markdown math is displayed as code instead of typeset formulas
impact: Technical explanations containing fractions, matrices or aligned equations remain raw TeX-like text and are harder to read.
recommendation: Add an optional math rendering path with literal fallback and source-preserving copy. This is a capability choice beyond ADR 0038's narrower work-group contract, not evidence that the recent styling migration failed.
acceptance: Inline fractions and display matrices render correctly in both themes. Partial invalid streaming remains readable. Copy returns the source equation and wide formulas remain keyboard-scrollable.

title: Transcript Markdown has no inline audio or video playback
impact: Generated or referenced audio and video require leaving the transcript. Image-style media references cannot become the inline players T3 provides.
recommendation: Classify media references before image rendering and provide accessible native playback or an intentional media attachment fallback. Treat this as optional parity investment according to the product's media workflows.
acceptance: An MP3 and an MP4 referenced in an assistant answer each expose playback controls or a labeled open action. Failed media does not appear as an unexplained broken image. Playback stops appropriately when its transcript is released.

title: Errors occupy an inline text row with repetitive recovery copy
impact: Failure details compete with the page and can wrap through much of a narrow panel. The recovery action is described in text rather than placed beside the message.
recommendation: Classify load, HTTP, engine, and profile errors. Give each a short summary and relevant action, with details behind disclosure. Keep layout stable and decide whether the failed page is meaningfully annotatable.
acceptance: Offline, refused connection, HTTP error, and unavailable engine each show one concise explanation and the correct retry/repair action at narrow panel widths, without repeated recovery sentences.

title: There is no prompt stash independent of the active draft
impact: Users cannot temporarily set aside several prompts and their context while composing something else. Per-thread autosave and sent-prompt history do not provide this workflow.
recommendation: Treat stash as an optional product addition after draft durability. Reuse structured draft snapshots and explicit deletion/retention rules.
acceptance: Stash two prompts including images and quotes, restart, compose a third, then restore either stash. No item sends implicitly and attachment expiry/failure is visible.

title: The native composer lacks rich Markdown and code-block editing
impact: Formatting is plain source text with token highlighting. Users do not get T3 list continuation, task nesting, code indentation, syntax highlighting or language selection while composing.
recommendation: Keep plain text as a supported choice. If richer editing is desired, first define exact Markdown round-trip and shortcut behavior, especially Enter inside code.
acceptance: Lists nest/continue predictably, code blocks indent and choose language, and toggling rich/plain preserves the exact submitted Markdown. Test IME, Unicode, multiline selection and undo across formatting boundaries.

title: There is no integrated voice-input workflow
impact: T3 users can dictate into a draft with recording, transcription and cancellation feedback. Ferrite has no corresponding composer control or state. OS-level dictation may still work and was not tested.
recommendation: Treat this as a product capability choice. If added, reuse explicit draft ownership and cancellation rules; disclose the transcription destination.
acceptance: Start voice input, dictate, finish, and verify text lands at the saved selection without sending. Cancel and microphone failure preserve the original draft. Changing threads does not insert text into the wrong draft.

title: A first prompt cannot fan out to multiple chosen models
impact: A user comparing models must manually create and submit several threads. T3 has a single draft action that launches selected models in isolated worktrees.
recommendation: Keep this optional and separate from ordinary send. If adopted, model a fan-out submission explicitly instead of overloading one thread binding.
acceptance: Send one draft to two models. Two isolated, clearly labeled threads receive identical prompt/context. Failure of one leaves its submission recoverable without resending the successful one.

title: Factory schedules do not offer one-time or sub-hour scheduled prompts
impact: Optional T3 parity gap for lightweight reminders or frequent prompts. Ferrite already supports recurring Factory automation and should not be described as lacking scheduling.
recommendation: Make an explicit product decision about lightweight thread scheduling. If adopted, add one-time scheduling and destination selection while preserving missed/overlap policies.
acceptance: An adopted one-time task runs once after restart, shows its destination and result, and does not silently repeat or duplicate an active run.

title: No first-class guest thread participation was found
impact: Optional collaboration gap. No discovered Ferrite entry point lets another person view one thread and propose owner-approved messages.
recommendation: Prioritize after broken primary workflows. If collaboration is adopted, define read scope, expiry, revocation and owner approval before exposing a share control.
acceptance: If adopted, the guest sees only the intended thread, proposed messages await owner action, and revocation ends access. Otherwise document the deliberate product boundary.
review_note: The absence claim remains an inference from bounded repository searches, not proof that every possible external collaboration route is impossible.

title: T3 device panels have no Ferrite panel counterpart
impact: Optional mobile-development parity gap. Ferrite's panel model has no embedded iOS or Android device tab; external provider device tools remain possible.
recommendation: Treat as a product boundary until current panel/browser interactions are reliable. If adopted, use the existing tab identity and focus model.
acceptance: An adopted device opens one identified tab, repeated opens activate it, device input remains scoped, and disconnect/reconnect is visible without breaking other panel focus.

title: Popover and menu entrances are globally disabled
impact: Model and other popovers, context menus, slash commands and mention menus appear and disappear instantly.
recommendation: Separate menus and popovers in the policy, add a short origin-aware entrance and retained noninteractive exit where requested, and preserve immediate keyboard selection. A global MENU_IN duration change alone does not implement exits.
acceptance: Open and close model, attachment, slash, mention, project-filter and context menus at every window edge. Verify the entrance originates at the anchor, closing immediately releases input, and rapid reopen does not show duplicate faces.

title: Long programmatic scrolls can snap before their final ease
impact: A distant jump to the latest content can teleport across most history and animate only the last viewport. A send target that has no measured bounds can land immediately.
recommendation: Decide and document a long-distance policy. If full spatial continuity is required, use measured estimates or staged movement that respects virtualization. If a shortened jump is desired, make that intentional and verify it visually instead of describing every jump as smooth.
acceptance: From several screens above the tail, activate Scroll to end and record the first frame through completion. Repeat a send with an unmeasured target. The observed path must match the chosen policy and remain interruptible.

title: Several transient elements animate in but disappear immediately
impact: Find bars, notices and background-work lines have asymmetric lifecycle feedback; layout can change abruptly on dismissal or completion.
recommendation: Use a small retained exit where it helps the user track completion or dismissal. Release hit testing immediately, and collapse occupied space in the same transition. Keep high-frequency text updates and direct manipulation immediate.
acceptance: Dismiss find, resolve a notice, finish background work, and remove an attachment while the composer is populated. Verify stable focus and intentional exit behavior without duplicate controls or hidden clickable remnants.

title: Timeline reverses the backend order and has no ordering control
impact: New activity appears at the bottom of a long discussion despite the panel documenting newest-first behavior.
recommendation: Remove the accidental reversal or define a shared order contract and add a user preference.
acceptance: With comments at 09:00 and 10:00, the default Timeline begins with 10:00. Any oldest-first option visibly changes the order.

title: Appearance is deliberately dark-only with fixed font families
impact: Users cannot choose a light/system theme, import a theme, or adjust interface and monospace font families independently. Transcript size and notification customization do exist.
recommendation: Keep the distinction visible in the parity inventory. Revisit dark-only and typography scope based on user preference rather than copying T3's whole theme editor.
acceptance: If expanded, change appearance and fonts, restart and inspect transcript, composer, menus, terminal and settings at representative sizes. If scope stays fixed, documentation accurately states the supported choices.

title: Pin as chapter is a transient label without chapter navigation
impact: The menu promises a way to mark a useful answer, but there is no chapter list to retrieve it and a new transcript view starts with no pins.
recommendation: Either complete persistent chapter navigation using stable message identities or remove this incomplete menu action until its purpose is supported. This is Ferrite's own incomplete feature, not a requirement inferred from T3.
acceptance: Pin an answer, restart, open the same thread and use a chapter list to jump to it. If the feature is intentionally temporary, the action name and feedback explicitly say so.
